context: Recall that a branching is a special case of a b-branching where b(v) = 1 for each v ∈ V . Indeed, by putting b(v) = 1 for each v ∈ V in (1) and (2), we obtain (3) and (4), respectively. As stated in Section 1, a maximum-weight branching can be found by a multi-phase greedy algorithm [4, 6, 11, 23], which appears in standard textbooks such as [35, 36, 47]. To the best of our knowledge, we have no other nontrivial special case of matroid intersection which can be solved greedily. For example, intersection of two partition matroids is equivalent to bipartite matching. This seems the simplest nontrivial example of matroid intersection, but we do not know a greedy algorithm for finding a maximum bipartite matching.
